sprintGoal: Add an opt-in agentic graph-reasoning loop to memclaw_recall, inspired by MRAgent's typed multi-tool query-time reasoning (Ji-shuo/MRAgent): instead of always doing one fixed hybrid-scored retrieval + fixed <=2-hop graph boost, an explicit reasoning_mode=true param lets the LLM pick from typed graph-query tools (by keyword, by graph-context, by time range, by entity links) across up to 3 turns to better answer relational/temporal questions. Must be strictly additive: default reasoning_mode=false path is byte-identical to today's call sequence (no latency regression on the documented 23ms p50 benchmark), and reasoning_mode=true only adds boosted ids on top of the existing single-pass result, never replaces it.

acceptanceCriteria: New file core-api/src/core_api/services/graph_query_tools.py defines query_by_keyword, query_by_graph_context, query_by_time_range, query_by_entity_links as async functions with a consistent (memory_ids: list[str], entity_ids: list[str], note: str) return shape
query_by_keyword wraps extract_entity_tokens() + storage_client.fts_search_entities() (storage_client.py:1218) — no new SQL, no new storage endpoint
query_by_graph_context wraps memory_service.expand_graph() (memory_service.py:2594), which itself calls storage_client.expand_graph() (storage_client.py:1221)

Each wrapper catches its own exceptions and returns ([], [], '<tool>: error - <msg>') rather than raising, so a single bad tool call cannot abort the loop

workItems.objective: Create graph_reasoning_loop.py implementing run_reasoning_loop(): a bounded, never-raising multi-turn loop that asks the LLM to pick a typed tool each turn (via complete_json), executes it, and accumulates boosted memory ids and a boost factor.
acceptanceCriteria: New file core-api/src/core_api/services/graph_reasoning_loop.py defines async def run_reasoning_loop(query: str, tenant_id: str, config, seed_entity_ids: list[str]) -> tuple[set[str], float, list[dict]] returning (boosted_memory_ids, boost_factor, trace)

New constants GRAPH_REASONING_MAX_ITERATIONS = 3, GRAPH_REASONING_STEP_TIMEOUT_SECONDS, GRAPH_REASONING_TOTAL_TIMEOUT_SECONDS defined in this module (not per-org configurable in v1, per plan scope decision)

Each turn builds a prompt listing TOOL_SPECS from graph_query_tools.py plus a 'done' option, calls LLMProvider.complete_json(prompt, response_schema={'tool': str, 'args': dict}) via call_with_fallback (common/llm/retry.py), same pattern recall_service.summarize_memories() already uses
Loop stops when the model returns tool='done', when GRAPH_REASONING_MAX_ITERATIONS is reached, or when the total-timeout asyncio.wait_for fires

Any exception raised by the LLM call, JSON parsing, or a tool wrapper is caught inside the loop; the function returns whatever (boosted_memory_ids, boost_factor, trace) has been accumulated so far and never propagates the exception to the caller
trace is a list of {turn, tool, args, result_count} dicts usable for diagnostic mode
Unit-testable in isolation: run_reasoning_loop accepts an injected llm/provider argument (or resolves via the same seam call_with_fallback uses) so tests can supply a scripted provider

reasons: Genuinely new orchestration pattern — no existing multi-turn tool-calling loop in-repo to copy
Must never raise or hang, since it will sit in the recall path once wired in RL-03 — bounded by both iteration count and asyncio.wait_for timeout
New file only in this task; still has zero effect on production until RL-03 wires it in

acceptanceCriteria: GROUNDING CORRECTION (found during /sprint-run execution, pre-dating any RL-03 code): _USE_PIPELINE_SEARCH = True is hardcoded in memory_service.py (line 96), so search_memories() always dispatches to _search_memories_pipeline() and _search_memories_legacy() is dead/unreachable code. The plan's original premise that _entity_boost_pipeline() (memory_service.py) is the live entity-boost mechanism was wrong — the real live boost step is ParallelEmbedAndEntityBoost in core-api/src/core_api/pipeline/steps/search/parallel_embed_entity_boost.py, run as step 4 of 11 inside build_search_pipeline() (core-api/src/core_api/pipeline/compositions/search.py). It returns the identical shape the plan assumed: (boosted_memory_ids: set[UUID], memory_boost_factor: dict[UUID, float]), written to ctx.data['boosted_memory_ids'] / ctx.data['memory_boost_factor']. SECOND CORRECTION: the plan's call chain via recall_service.recall() is also wrong — recall_service.recall() (recall_service.py:225) has zero production callers anywhere in the repo (confirmed via grep across core-api/src). Both mcp_server.memclaw_recall (mcp_server.py:678) and the REST /recall endpoint (routes/memories.py:~1584-1613) call memory_service.search_memories() + recall_service.summarize_memories() directly, per an explicit prior audit fix (P3, see mcp_server.py:633-641 comment) that avoids holding a DB session across the LLM brief round-trip and avoids a duplicate search call. recall_service.recall() is dead code. This acceptance criteria set targets the corrected, real wiring point. _search_memories_legacy(), memory_service._entity_boost_pipeline(), and recall_service.recall() are NOT touched by this task (dead code — touching them would violate the orphan/surgical-changes rule).

memclaw_recall MCP tool handler in mcp_server.py (async def memclaw_recall, mcp_server.py:574) accepts reasoning_mode: bool = False and passes it directly into its existing search_memories(...) call (mcp_server.py:678) as reasoning_mode=reasoning_mode

memory_service.search_memories() gains reasoning_mode: bool = False and forwards it into _search_memories_pipeline(), which adds 'reasoning_mode': reasoning_mode to the PipelineContext(data={...}) dict; when reasoning_mode is False, ctx.data['reasoning_mode'] is False/absent and the new pipeline step below is a single dict-lookup no-op — same call sequence and latency as today

New file core-api/src/core_api/pipeline/steps/search/graph_reasoning_boost.py defines class GraphReasoningBoost with name 'graph_reasoning_boost' and async execute(self, ctx): if not ctx.data.get('reasoning_mode') or not ctx.data.get('graph_expand', True): return None (or StepResult(outcome=StepOutcome.SKIPPED)) immediately — mirrors the graph_expand gating parallel_embed_entity_boost.py already uses

When reasoning_mode and graph_expand are both true, GraphReasoningBoost awaits graph_reasoning_loop.run_reasoning_loop(...) and unions its boosted_memory_ids into ctx.data['boosted_memory_ids'], combining per-memory boost via max() against ctx.data['memory_boost_factor'] (never multiplied or replaced), and stores the trace at ctx.data['reasoning_trace']
compositions/search.py's build_search_pipeline() inserts GraphReasoningBoost() immediately after ParallelEmbedAndEntityBoost() in the step list — the other 10 steps and their order are unchanged

diagnostic=True responses include ctx.data.get('reasoning_trace') under a reasoning_trace key in diagnostic_ctx (populated in _search_memories_pipeline()'s existing diagnostic-extraction block) when reasoning_mode was used, absent otherwise

grep for 'ParallelEmbedAndEntityBoost()' and 'GraphReasoningBoost()' in compositions/search.py confirms exactly one insertion point and no other composition (e.g. any STM-only pipeline) was accidentally changed
